title: Hanuman's first words
hook: a stranger's sentence so well made that Rama names every virtue in it
carry: true, kind, helpful speech is a practice

segments.voice: Yesterday: Hanuman walked down the mountain as a bhikshu, to calm a frightened king. Call on Hanuman when you're afraid. Today the week closes.

Have you ever met someone and known within a minute, from how they spoke, that you could trust them? Not from what they said, exactly. From how. Hanuman reaches the brothers and speaks, and when he's finished, Rama turns to Lakshmana and says something remarkable about a stranger's sentence. Remember where Rama is. He has lost his kingdom, his father and now his wife. He has no reason to trust anyone on this mountain. And a few sentences from a stranger change that.
screen: `NOT WHAT, BUT HOW.` → `RAMA TURNS TO LAKSHMANA.`

segments.voice: Hanuman greets them with respect. You look like sages, he says, or like kings: why are you in this forest? Then he tells them who he is: a minister of Sugriva, a monkey king driven out by his brother, who wants their friendship. He's careful and warm, and honest about who sent him. Then Rama turns to Lakshmana, and his praise is precise. Nobody could speak like this, he says, who hadn't learned the Rig Veda, the Yajur Veda and the Sama Veda. He has clearly studied grammar well; in all he said, not one word was wrong. Nothing in his face, his eyes or his brow was out of place. He didn't drag it out or rush it. His voice came from the chest and throat, in a middle pitch, clear and pleasing. A king with a messenger like this, Rama says, can get anything done. Notice what Rama praises: not strength, but speech. Hinduism takes speech this seriously on purpose. In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna names a tapas, a discipline, of speech: words that cause no distress, that are true, pleasing and helpful, together with steady study of sacred texts. That's Hanuman on this mountain. He doesn't flatter or rush, he's honest about who sent him, and his learning shows. It's one reason devotees honor Hanuman for wisdom and eloquence, not just strength. And the alliance that will find Sita begins right here, with a sentence.
screen: `A MINISTER OF SUGRIVA.` · `NOT ONE WORD WRONG.` · `NOT TOO LONG, NOT RUSHED.` · `THE TAPAS OF SPEECH: TRUE, KIND, HELPFUL.` · then, large: `A SENTENCE THAT STARTS A FRIENDSHIP.`

segments.voice: Choose one true, kind sentence you need to say to someone soon. Run it past the Gita's checks: does it cause no needless hurt, is it true, is it pleasant, does it help? Shape it, a word too many, a tone not quite right, and say it again in your head a little cleaner, until it passes and rests easy.
Vakya, a sentence: what Rama praises in Hanuman, and what the Gita asks to be true, kind and helpful.
Your line: true, kind, helpful speech is a practice. Rama heard a friend in the way a stranger spoke. That's day five hundred eighty-one.
